correctness.rationale: The source-derived binary deletion-distance identity h=2+max(r+ell) is applied with four completely explicit runwise distance sums. All four positive run-length boundaries, including b=1 and c=1, are represented. The derived decoupling h=max(g(a,c),g(d,b)) gives two exactly independent weighted pair counts; their product is the stated polynomial. Direct greedy-subsequence BFS checks 4096 quadruples independently, direct subword sets check 8192 insertions, and coefficient enumerations check H=3..11. Finite tests are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: For piecewise-testable singleton languages, wordwise height specifies the maximum subsequence length needed to identify an exact word. The result enumerates *all* binary four-run words by height and length, not just selected samples; the unexpected square reflects separability of opposite-run constraints and includes singleton exceptions. It yields exact counts at every finite length and every threshold, useful as a structural benchmark for short run-length compressed strings. This is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary finite cutoff, and does not claim a general downstream theorem.
